_comment: Network-position credential-access actions: LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning (Responder), NTLM relay (ntlmrelayx), and IPv6 DNS takeover (mitm6). These are ACTIVE, noisy, on-the-wire techniques, they are gated on a Windows/AD network context and marked autonomy:manual, so `obol cruise` never fires them: it surfaces each as a recommended move and PAUSES for the operator, who runs the copy-paste command and pastes the output back (Responder's captured NetNTLMv2 hashes parse into hash.ntlm crackable material). obol stages/recommends; the operator pulls the trigger. Each carries its report finding (llmnr-nbtns-poisoning / ntlm-relay / ipv6-dns-takeover).

actions.title: Validate A Found Credential
actions.hypothesis: You hold a credential you FOUND rather than cracked: a password in a config, a reused guess, a secret from a share. You have not proven it actually authenticates anywhere yet, so one switchless nxc check confirms whether it works, and over which protocol, before you build anything on it. A credential you cracked from a hash, bruteforced online, or already logged in with is proven, so this step quietly disappears for those.
actions.proves: that a found credential authenticates, and over which protocol (SMB, LDAP, WinRM, RDP)
actions.does_not_prove: what the credential can DO once it works, that is the enumeration and access moves it unlocks; and (Pwn3d!) aside, whether it is a local admin

commands.note: The switchless validation: no module, no action, just connect and authenticate. A [+] line means the password works here; a [-] with STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE means it does not. (Pwn3d!) also tells you the account is a local admin. Do this before you spend the credential on anything.
Same check for a found NT hash instead of a password, pass-the-hash. A [+] means the hash authenticates; you never needed the plaintext.
Confirm the same credential over LDAP, which you need for BloodHound collection and directory queries even when SMB is locked down.
Confirm WinRM: a [+] here means an interactive shell is one evil-winrm away. This is the fastest path to a foothold once the credential checks out.

actions.title: LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning (Responder)
actions.hypothesis: On a Windows broadcast network, hosts fall back to LLMNR/NBT-NS/mDNS to resolve names. Responder answers those broadcasts, so a mistyped path or an auto-connect hands over a NetNTLMv2 hash to crack offline (or relay). Active on the wire, run it, wait, crack; never auto-fired.
actions.proves: captured NetNTLMv2 challenge-response hashes (crackable material) when a host authenticated to the poisoned name
actions.does_not_prove: access or pass-the-hash, a NetNTLMv2 capture is crack-only material, not an NT hash and not a validated login

commands.note: Analyse mode first, observe which LLMNR/NBT-NS/mDNS names are being queried WITHOUT poisoning, so you know the network is noisy before you answer.
Poison + capture (WPAD on, verbose). Leave it running; captured NetNTLMv2 hashes land in the console and under /usr/share/responder/logs/. Paste them back to obol.

actions.title: NTLM Relay (ntlmrelayx)
actions.hypothesis: When SMB signing is NOT required (see the NTLM Relay finding), captured NTLM authentication can be relayed to another host instead of cracked, dumping SAM, executing a command, or adding a computer. Pair with Responder (SMB/HTTP servers off) or mitm6 as the capture source.
actions.proves: a relay lead, a foothold path when the relayed identity has rights on the target
actions.does_not_prove: access on its own, the relayed identity must have privileges on the relay target

commands.note: Relay to a list of signing-disabled hosts; dumps SAM by default. relay-targets.txt = the hosts from your scope where signing is off.
Relay to one host and open an interactive SMB client (-i) on success.

commands.run: sudo responder -I {{iface}} -wv   # first: set SMB=Off and HTTP=Off in /etc/responder/Responder.conf
commands.note: Turn Responder's own SMB/HTTP servers off so the auth is relayed by ntlmrelayx instead of captured.

actions.title: IPv6 DNS Takeover (mitm6)
actions.hypothesis: Windows prefers IPv6 and asks for a DHCPv6 lease it usually doesn't get. mitm6 answers as the rogue DHCPv6 + DNS server, becoming the victim's DNS, then relays the resulting authentication (via ntlmrelayx) to LDAP/S on a DC. High-impact on a default AD network; noisy and active.
actions.proves: an IPv6-relay lead into AD (e.g. adding a computer / delegating) when relayed to a DC
actions.does_not_prove: access on its own, the outcome depends on the relayed identity's AD rights

commands.note: Become the rogue DHCPv6/DNS server for the domain on your attacker interface. Run alongside the ntlmrelayx command below.
Relay the mitm6-driven auth to LDAPS on the DC ({{target}}); -wh serves a fake WPAD. Loot lands in ./loot.
